topics.title: AI + ML Foundations
topics.description: Build intuition around AI, ML data, and first prediction concepts.

lessons.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML
lessons.body: Artificial intelligence is the broad goal of building systems that perform intelligent tasks, while machine learning is a subset that learns patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules.

lessons.title: Data types: structured vs unstructured data
lessons.body: Structured data follows a fixed schema such as rows and columns, while unstructured data (text, audio, images) needs additional processing before models can consume it effectively.

lessons.title: Intro to datasets
lessons.body: A dataset is a collection of examples used for training and evaluation, typically with features (inputs) and labels (targets) when the task is supervised.

lessons.title: Basic math for AI
lessons.body: Core AI math includes vectors, matrix operations, and basic algebra because model predictions are usually computed as weighted combinations of numeric features.

lessons.title: Intro to statistics
lessons.body: Statistics helps quantify uncertainty through concepts like mean, variance, and distributions, which are essential for understanding noisy real-world data.

lessons.title: Visualization basics
lessons.body: Visualizations like histograms, scatter plots, and box plots quickly reveal distribution shape, outliers, and variable relationships before modeling begins.

lessons.title: Data inspection
lessons.body: Initial data inspection checks missing values, duplicates, data types, and unrealistic ranges to prevent avoidable modeling errors.

lessons.title: Intro to predictions
lessons.body: A prediction is a model output produced from input features, such as a class label, a probability, or a continuous numeric estimate.

lessons.title: Supervised vs unsupervised
lessons.body: Supervised learning trains with labeled targets, while unsupervised learning finds latent structure such as clusters or low-dimensional representations without labels.

lessons.title: Feature vs label
lessons.body: Features are the inputs provided to a model, and the label is the ground-truth value the model is trained to predict.

lessons.title: Data cleaning basics
lessons.body: Data cleaning standardizes formats, handles nulls, removes duplicates, and corrects inconsistencies so the model learns from reliable signals.

lessons.title: Simple classification idea
lessons.body: Classification maps an input to one of several classes, for example spam vs not spam, often using probabilities and a decision threshold.

lessons.title: Simple regression idea
lessons.body: Regression estimates a continuous value such as demand or price and is evaluated with error-based metrics like MAE or RMSE.

lessons.title: AI workflows
lessons.body: A practical AI workflow moves from problem framing and data preparation to training, evaluation, deployment, and continuous monitoring.

lessons.title: AI use cases
lessons.body: Common AI use cases include recommendation, fraud detection, forecasting, language understanding, and visual inspection in production systems.

topics.title: Core Machine Learning Models
topics.description: Learn beginner ML algorithms, evaluation, and first project workflow.

lessons.title: Linear regression
lessons.body: Linear regression models a continuous target as a weighted sum of features and is a strong baseline for interpretable numeric prediction tasks.

lessons.title: Logistic regression
lessons.body: Logistic regression transforms a linear score into a probability and is commonly used for binary classification with a clear decision boundary.

lessons.title: Train/test split
lessons.body: A train/test split keeps one partition unseen during training so final metrics reflect how the model behaves on new data.

lessons.title: Basic metrics
lessons.body: Classification metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 complement accuracy, while regression uses MAE, MSE, or RMSE depending on error sensitivity.

lessons.title: k-NN algorithm
lessons.body: k-NN predicts using the labels of nearby examples, so performance depends strongly on distance scaling and the choice of k.

lessons.title: Decision trees
lessons.body: Decision trees recursively split features into rules, making predictions easy to explain but often requiring pruning or ensembles to avoid overfitting.

lessons.title: Data preprocessing
lessons.body: Preprocessing includes normalization, encoding categorical values, and handling missing data so model inputs are consistent and learnable.

lessons.title: Feature engineering
lessons.body: Feature engineering creates informative inputs from raw data, such as ratios, time features, or domain-derived aggregates that improve model signal.

lessons.title: Clustering basics
lessons.body: Clustering groups similar samples without labels, helping with segmentation, anomaly exploration, and dataset understanding.

lessons.title: PCA basics
lessons.body: Principal Component Analysis projects data to lower dimensions while preserving maximum variance, useful for compression and denoising.

lessons.title: Pipeline basics
lessons.body: ML pipelines chain preprocessing and modeling steps into one reproducible workflow, reducing leakage and training-serving inconsistencies.

lessons.title: Overfitting concept
lessons.body: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise from training data, causing strong train performance but weak generalization to unseen examples.

lessons.title: Cross-validation
lessons.body: Cross-validation rotates validation folds to estimate performance more reliably and to compare models with less split-to-split variance.

lessons.title: Model evaluation workflow
lessons.body: A good evaluation workflow defines metrics upfront, checks baseline comparisons, inspects error patterns, and validates assumptions before deployment.

lessons.title: First ML project
lessons.body: A first ML project should prioritize clear problem scope, clean data, a simple baseline, and iterative improvements guided by measurable outcomes.

topics.title: Modeling and System Building
topics.description: Go deeper into model quality, neural methods, and deployment-minded workflows.

lessons.title: Ensemble methods
lessons.body: Ensembles combine multiple models to improve robustness and accuracy by averaging or boosting complementary prediction behaviors.

lessons.title: Hyperparameter tuning
lessons.body: Hyperparameter tuning explores settings like depth, learning rate, and regularization to maximize validation performance without overfitting.

lessons.title: Feature selection
lessons.body: Feature selection removes redundant or noisy variables, improving interpretability, reducing training cost, and sometimes improving generalization.

lessons.title: Bias-variance tradeoff
lessons.body: The bias-variance tradeoff balances underfitting and overfitting: simpler models have higher bias, complex models often have higher variance.

lessons.title: Advanced evaluation
lessons.body: Advanced evaluation includes calibration, threshold analysis, subgroup metrics, and cost-aware decision rules for production-relevant model assessment.

lessons.title: Neural networks basics
lessons.body: Neural networks stack differentiable layers that transform input features into richer representations learned from data.

lessons.title: Backpropagation
lessons.body: Backpropagation computes gradients efficiently from output to input layers, enabling gradient-based optimization of neural network parameters.

lessons.title: Deep learning basics
lessons.body: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks to automatically learn hierarchical features in text, vision, and speech tasks.

lessons.title: NLP basics
lessons.body: NLP converts human language into machine-readable representations for tasks such as classification, extraction, translation, and generation.

lessons.title: Computer vision basics
lessons.body: Computer vision models process images with spatial filters to detect patterns such as edges, objects, and scene context.

lessons.title: Time series basics
lessons.body: Time series modeling respects temporal order and often uses lags, trends, and seasonality features to forecast future values.

lessons.title: Recommendation systems
lessons.body: Recommendation systems rank items by predicted relevance using collaborative signals, content features, or hybrid methods.

lessons.title: Model deployment basics
lessons.body: Deployment packages a trained model behind an API or batch job with versioning, monitoring, and rollback safety.

lessons.title: Data pipelines
lessons.body: Data pipelines automate ingestion, validation, transformation, and feature generation so training and inference use consistent data logic.

lessons.title: Model interpretability
lessons.body: Interpretability techniques such as feature importance and SHAP explain model behavior for trust, debugging, and compliance.

topics.title: Production-Grade AI
topics.description: Master advanced architectures, scaling techniques, and responsible AI operations.

lessons.title: Deep learning architectures
lessons.body: Different architectures specialize in different data modalities: CNNs for images, transformers for sequences, and recurrent variants for temporal patterns.

lessons.title: Transfer learning
lessons.body: Transfer learning adapts pretrained models to new tasks with less labeled data by reusing representations learned at scale.

lessons.title: NLP advanced
lessons.body: Advanced NLP covers tokenization strategy, attention-based architectures, fine-tuning, and evaluation beyond simple accuracy metrics.

lessons.title: Computer vision advanced
lessons.body: Advanced vision topics include object detection, segmentation, augmentation policy design, and domain shift handling.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning
lessons.body: Reinforcement learning trains agents to maximize cumulative reward by learning policies from environment interaction.

lessons.title: Generative AI
lessons.body: Generative AI models learn data distributions to create new content such as text, images, or audio that follows observed patterns.

lessons.title: Large language models
lessons.body: LLMs are transformer-based models trained on massive corpora to perform reasoning, retrieval-augmented tasks, and controlled generation.

lessons.title: MLOps
lessons.body: MLOps applies software engineering discipline to ML systems through CI/CD, reproducible training, monitoring, and governance.

lessons.title: Distributed training
lessons.body: Distributed training splits data and computation across multiple devices to reduce training time for large models.

lessons.title: AutoML
lessons.body: AutoML automates model search, feature processing, and tuning to speed up baseline creation while preserving reproducibility.

lessons.title: Graph neural networks
lessons.body: Graph neural networks propagate information across node neighborhoods, making them effective for relational data like networks and molecules.

lessons.title: Multimodal AI
lessons.body: Multimodal models align and fuse modalities such as text and images to solve tasks requiring cross-modal understanding.

lessons.title: Model optimization
lessons.body: Model optimization techniques like quantization, pruning, and distillation reduce latency and memory while preserving acceptable accuracy.

lessons.title: AI ethics
lessons.body: AI ethics addresses fairness, transparency, privacy, and accountability to reduce harm and align systems with human values.

lessons.title: End-to-end system
lessons.body: An end-to-end AI system integrates data, training, deployment, monitoring, and feedback loops into one reliable production lifecycle.
